title: A Fish Caught in 1827 Weighed 3,463 Pounds. Nothing Since Has Come Close
subject: beluga sturgeon

scenes.text: A fish caught in 1827 weighed more than a small car. Nothing since has come close.
It was a female beluga sturgeon from the Volga. Twenty-three feet long, 3,463 pounds.
Belugas can live over a hundred years, and females don't breed until they're about fifteen.
That's the problem. Their eggs are caviar, and fishing took the oldest, biggest fish first.
Dams block the rivers too. Their spawning trips have been up to 1,000 kilometers upstream.
Today the beluga is critically endangered. A giant like that may never swim again.

description:
A beluga sturgeon caught in the Volga estuary in 1827 weighed 1,571 kilograms, 3,463 pounds, and measured 7.2 meters. It's the largest accepted record.
These fish can live over a century, mature slowly, are prized for caviar, and are now critically endangered.
Have you ever seen a sturgeon in the wild?
first_comment: Would a fish this big still exist if we hadn't fished the giants first? Tell me below.
